summary: Melanippus (Ancient Greek: Μελάνιππος), son of Hicetaon, is a Trojan champion from Percote who dwelt in Priam's house once the war began. Homer has Hector chide him among the kinsmen at the ships; Nestor spears him and Antilochus strips his armour. He is one of several Iliadic Melanippi.

sections.heading: Hicetaon's son of Percote
paragraphs: Strabo and the Homeric scholia place Melanippus among Hicetaon's sons (brother of Thymoetes and others). He pastured cattle at Percote until the Danaans came, then lived as a foremost Trojan under Priam. In Iliad 15 Hector urges him into the fight; Nestor strikes him beside the nipple and Antilochus takes the spoils.
Wikipedia and the poem also know a Priamid Melanippus slain by Teucer and yet another Trojan killed by Patroclus — separate atlas nodes where entered.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Not the Theban Melanippus son of Astacus (Seven Against Thebes), not Melanippus of Patrae, not the Achaean gift-bearer, nor melanippus-trojan / melanippus-patroclus-roll / melanippus-achaean. The atlas id melanippus-hicetaonid is Hicetaon's Percotean son alone.
